messages:
olivia: FYI — AcmeHealth just escalated: several API requests from EU region are landing in us-west and p50 latency spiked from 80ms -> 650ms. Getting occasional 503s during failover. Ticket #CH-9821. Repro steps below.

samir: thanks. can you paste a request id and the exact curl you used? also which model/route?

olivia: request ids: r-2026-03-10-61a3, r-2026-03-10-61a4. Route: /v1/generate model: redwood-2-large. curl i used: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "X-Region: eu-central-1" \
  -d '{"prompt":"test","max_tokens":40}'
```
When X-Region header is set to eu-central-1, traffic still goes to us-west per trace.

support-bot: Auto-detected anomaly: region_mismatch_rate > 0.05 for customer AcmeHealth in eu-central-1 window=15m. Created incident ink-1751.

anya: quick triage — this smells like failover policy ordering/weights. we recently merged a change that introduced per-customer overrides + sticky routing TTLs. if sticky routing is enabled and priority list has a non-zero weight for us-west earlier, requests can stick to wrong region on cold starts.

dave: do we have the customer's failover policy? olivia — can you paste the policy id?

olivia: policy id fpolicy-acme-332. here's the policy snippet from config service (sanitized):
```
{
  "policy_id": "fpolicy-acme-332",
  "targets": [
    {"region":"us-west-2","priority":1,"weight":50},
    {"region":"eu-central-1","priority":2,"weight":100}
  ],
  "sticky_ttl_secs": 86400
}
```

samir: aha — priority=1 is us-west. so even though weight for eu-central is higher, priority takes precedence for routing. sticky_ttl=24h will keep clients pinned to us-west if they hit it. this is probably the misconfiguration.

anya: exact. recent UI allowed editing weights without making priority ordering obvious. backend routing uses priority first, then weights within same priority bucket. the API docs are ambiguous here — will file doc bug.

olivia: agreed. customer says they didn't modify policy. possible rollout bug from the per-customer override migration we ran yesterday?

dave: infra-bot — can you show recent config pushes for fpolicy-acme-332?

infra-bot: config-service: push detected for fpolicy-acme-332 by deployer@infra at 2026-03-10T02:12:11Z. change set id cs-7784. Diff: priority order swapped for targets (eu <-> us-west).

samir: that explains it. cs-7784 was the per-customer override migration. looks like we inadvertently inverted priority fields when converting older policies.

anya: mitigation plan: 1) hotfix migration to restore original priority ordering for affected customers. 2) temporarily reduce sticky_ttl for AcmeHealth to 0 to force re-evaluation/rehash. 3) communicate to customer and rollback if impact persists.

dave: i can push a targeted patch to config-service to flip priorities back for fpolicy-acme-332 and a script to scan other policies for inverted priorities. prepping CL now.

olivia: customer wants ETA — what's realistic?

samir: if dave pushes hotfix and infra runs it on prod config-service, we can patch AcmeHealth within ~30 min. then they need to re-run a few requests to repopulate routing. there will be some increased load on eu-central transiently.

anya: also change the routing logic urgently: when weights contradict priority intent, emit a warning and prevent sticky_ttl > 0 if priority lower region has higher weight. long-term: add a UI confirmation when editing priorities.

olivia: can you add repro steps for customer so they can test after patch? i'll send to them.

samir: repro steps: 1) set header X-Region: eu-central-1 in a short loop (see curl below) 2) check response header X-Served-Region 3) if X-Served-Region != eu-central-1 after patch, run `curl` again to force new sticky assignment.

olivia: curl snippet: 
```
for i in {1..5}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "X-Region: eu-central-1" \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"ping","max_tokens":2}' -D - | grep X-Served-Region;
  sleep 1;
done
```

infra-bot: Scheduling config roll: cs-7784-revert targeted -> prod. estimated start 2026-03-10T02:48:00Z.

dave: CL uploaded: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/config-service/+/diffs/1234. roll planned now. i'll watch metrics.

olivia: customer notified: we told them we're investigating and expect a fix within 30-45m. keeping them on the phone.

samir: postmortem items: - migration validation: ensure priority fields preserved - add integration test catching inverted priorities - improve observability: surface region mismatch root cause in console - docs: clarify priority vs weight semantics

anya: tagging eng-ml and product to update docs + UI. also add a short-lived alert to detect sticky_ttl > 0 with priority inversion.

olivia: will update ticket CH-9821 with repro, logs, and tentative timeline. ping me if hotfix delays. :thumbsup:

dave: hotfix applied, metrics look good — match rate for eu-central requests -> 98% after retries. will keep monitoring for 2 hours.

olivia: confirmed with customer — back to normal, latency returned to baseline. they requested a writeup of cause and mitigation. i'll draft and circulate.

samir: great. closing incident after postmortem. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
